D17, D46. Stein et al. 2018 deposit only tree sets, from two dating scenarios (1 and 10 calibration fossils). Their Supplementary Information (41559_2017_448_MOESM1_ESM.pdf, p.2, l.26-28) designates the 10-fossil set: 'Both fossil scenarios yielded a similar root age of 349 - 488 MYA. Given these similarities in age estimates across the two fossil calibration scenarios, we focus on summarizing results from the 10-fossil calibration trees.' The set used is therefore data.vertlife.org/sharktree/10.cal.tree.nex (10,000 trees, sha256 0e447ede08914279332f8eb5a2d6bcdafe1ab7b5b1f00e00172886719b9e62e2). Its maximum-clade-credibility tree, by the rooted product of clade frequencies (the criterion of phangorn::maxCladeCred and TreeAnnotator), is tree 2043: log clade credibility -3737.13, next best -3743.96 (tree 5024); computed with Data/raw/revision-2026-10/sharks/mcc/mcc.py on whitebox (Data/raw/revision-2026-10/sharks/ten_calibration/mcc10.log), tree written with the translate table applied. Both scenarios draw root ages from the same lognormal density (accepted MS pp.16-17); root height over the 10,000 trees: 10-fossil median 377.83 Ma, central 95% 353.57-437.61, range 348.76-488.29; 1-fossil median 377.82, 353.43-437.50, range 348.86-488.08 (rootages.py); the source's '349 - 488 MYA' is that range. Supersedes the 1-fossil MCC tree 7847 used before round F3 (D43).
